key_insight: Replacing a random latent-to-text mapping with a learned diffusion language model produces lower-perplexity attack prompts while retaining the standard-Gaussian latent-space framework.
engineering_relevance: Black-box LLM risk assessments can depend strongly on the prompt-generation mapping, making language-grounded generation important for interpreting attack results.
method: Decode continuous Gaussian latents into text using a learned diffusion language model.
Preserve downstream sampling or optimization without the artificial random mapping.
Evaluate sampling-based RareTrap and optimization-based ThinkTrap.
evidence_signal: Character-level perplexity falls from 10^3–10^7 to 3–5 in RareTrap and from 20–28 to 4.3–5.4 in ThinkTrap; risk estimates can differ by an order of magnitude between mappings.
watch_item: Lower perplexity alone does not establish that prompts evade deployed guardrails or represent real-world malicious inputs.
paper_title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
